title: Indian House Price Prediction Project
text:
2 Columns in our dataset:
Some preliminary observations of the given dataset:

ID: Different rows having different Integer values.
State: Indian States ( character ).
City: Name of Cities ( character ).
Locality: Name of Localities ( character ).
Property_Type: There are 3 types of properties - Apartment, Independent House, Villa ( character ).
BHK: 5 varieties are there - 1,2,3,4,5 ( integer ).
Size_in_sqFt: Plot size in Sqft ( integer ).
Price_in_Lakhs: Price of the properties in Lakhs ( Double ).
Price_per_SqFt: Price of the properties per Sqft ( Double ).
Year_Built: Year in which the property was built ( integer ).
Furnished_Status: Status of furnishing - Furnished, Unfurnished, Semi-furnished ( character ).
Floor_No.: Floor No. ( Integer ).
Total_Floors: Total no. of floors ( Integer ).
Age_of_Property: Age of the property ( Integer ).
Nearby_Schools: No. of schools nearby ( Integer ).
Nearby_Hospitals: No. of hospitals nearby ( Integer ).
Public_Transport_Accessibility: Ease of accessing public transportation - High, Low, Medium ( character ).
Parking_Space: Availability of Parking space - Yes, No ( character ).
Security: Proper security system - Yes, No ( character ).
Amenities: Amenities like: Playground, Gym, Pool, etc. ( character ).
Facing: Orientation of the house - East, West, South, North ( character ).
Owner_Type: Type of owner - Owner, Builder, Broker ( character ).
Availability_Status: Status of availability - Ready_to_move, Under_construction ( character ).

title: Indian House Price Prediction Project
text:
3 Observations from the data

3.1 Pricing

Price_in_Lakhs = Size_in_SqFt × Price_per_SqFt + (Some dynamic charge/ discount )



Code
Price_diff <- dt$Price_in_Lakhs - (dt$Size_in_SqFt * dt$Price_per_SqFt)
typeof(dt$Size_in_SqFt)


[1] "integer"


Code
pos_price_diff = sum(round(Price_diff,4) > 0.0)
no_price_diff = sum(round(Price_diff,2) == 0.0)
neg_price_diff = sum(round(Price_diff,4) < 0.0)
print((pos_price_diff+no_price_diff+neg_price_diff))


[1] 250000


50.29% of the data has prices greater than the equation.
49.65% of the data has prices less than the equation.
0.05% of the data has exactly same value as the equation.


Code
# Predicting the rate (Price per SqFt) instead of total price
rate_model <- lm(Price_per_SqFt ~ Size_in_SqFt, data = dt)

# Plotting the relationship
plot(dt$Size_in_SqFt, dt$Price_per_SqFt, 
     pch = 16, col = rgb(0,0,1,0.1),
     main = "Relationship: Size vs Price per sqft",
     xlab = "Size in sqft", ylab = "Price per sqft")
abline(rate_model, col = "red", lwd = 2)










The plot displays a strong negative non-linear relationship, where the price per square foot drops sharply as property size increases before stabilizing for larger homes.

Code
#For Ready_to_Move House
yearly_mean_ready <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Year_Built,data = 
                                 dt[which(dt$Availability_Status  =="Ready_to_Move"), ], FUN = mean)

#For Under_Construction House
yearly_mean_cons <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Year_Built,data = 
                                 dt[which(dt$Availability_Status  =="Under_Construction"), ], FUN = mean)

library(plotly)

p <- plot_ly() %>%
  # Line for Ready to Move
  add_trace(data = yearly_mean_ready, x = ~Year_Built, y = ~Price_in_Lakhs, name = 'Ready_to_Move',
            type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines+markers', line = list(color = 'darkgreen')) %>%
  
  # Line for Under Construction
  add_trace(data = yearly_mean_cons, x = ~Year_Built, y = ~Price_in_Lakhs, name = 'Under_Construction',
            type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines+markers', line = list(color = 'blue', dash = 'dash')) %>%
  
  # Line for Overall Median
  add_trace(data = yearly_mean, x = ~Year_Built, y = ~Price_in_Lakhs, name = 'Overall Mean',
            type = 'scatter', mode = 'lines+markers', line = list(color = 'red', dash = 'dash')) %>%
  
  # Layout and Axis Titles
  layout(title = "Built-Year wise Mean Price Trends: Ready_to_Move vs Under_Construction",
         xaxis = list(title = "Year Built"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Price (in lakhs)", range = c(240, 270)),
         hovermode = "x unified") # Shows all values when hover over a year

# Display the plot
p

3.10 Age of Property


Code
# Calculate the age statistics
age_mean <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Age_of_Property, data = dt, FUN = mean)
age_min  <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Age_of_Property, data = dt, FUN = min)
age_max  <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Age_of_Property, data = dt, FUN = max)
age_median <- aggregate(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Age_of_Property, data = dt, FUN = median)

plot(age_mean$Age_of_Property, age_mean$Price_in_Lakhs, 
     type = "o", lty = 1,
     pch = 19,
     col = "darkgreen",
     xlab = "Age of property", 
     ylab = "Price (in lakhs)",ylim=c(246,259),
     main = "Age of property price trends: Mean vs Median")

lines(age_median$Age_of_Property, age_median$Price_in_Lakhs, 
     type = "o", lty = 2,
     pch = 19,
     col = "blue")

#Legend
legend("bottomright", 
       legend = c("Mean", "Median"),
       col = c("darkgreen", "blue"), 
       lty = c(1, 2), 
       pch = c(19, 19,19),
       bty = "n")










There is no consistent trend showing that prices increase or decrease with the age of the property, suggesting that age alone does not explain the variation of price and more analysis is required.

calculate_premium <- function(amenity_name) {
  # Mean price with the amenity
  mean_with <- mean(dt_expanded$Price_in_Lakhs[dt_expanded[[amenity_name]] == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Mean price without the amenity
  mean_without <- mean(dt_expanded$Price_in_Lakhs[dt_expanded[[amenity_name]] == 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate Premium
  premium_val <- mean_with - mean_without
  premium_pct <- (premium_val / mean_without) * 100
  
  
  data.frame(
    Amenity = amenity_name,
    Avg_Price_With = round(mean_with, 2),
    Avg_Price_Without = round(mean_without, 2),
    Premium_Lakhs = round(premium_val, 2),
    Premium_Percent = round(premium_pct, 2)
  )
}

4 Hypothesis Testing

4.1 Research Statement: The prices of villas are generally higher than the apartments.

NULL HYPOTHESIS:- The average prices of the apartments are equal to the average prices of the villas.
ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS:- The average prices of the villas are higher than the average prices of the apartments.
H0: mean_price_of_villa = mean_price_of_apartment
H1: mean _price_of_villa > mean_price_of_apartment


Code
t.test(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Property_Type,
       data = subset(dt, Property_Type %in% c("Villa","Apartment")),
       alternative = "greater")



    Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  Price_in_Lakhs by Property_Type
t = 1.2317, df = 166668, p-value = 0.109
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Apartment and group Villa is greater than 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -0.2862368        Inf
sample estimates:
mean in group Apartment     mean in group Villa 
               254.6221                253.7688 



Interpretation:-
Here the p-values are greater than 0.05, which implies that we failed to reject the null hypothesis. Thus, based on our data-set, we cannot conclude that the prices of villas are higher than that of apartments.
There is insufficient evidence to conclude that the average price of villas are higher than that of apartments.


4.2 Research Statement :- Do Furnished homes have more cost than the Unfurnished homes ?

NULL HYPOTHESIS:- The furnished and unfurnished houses have the same price.
ALTERNATIVE HYPOTHESIS:- The furnished houses have higher prices than the unfurnished houses


Code
subset_dt <- subset(dt, Furnished_Status %in% c("Furnished", "Unfurnished"))

t.test(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Furnished_Status,
       data = subset_dt)



    Welch Two Sample t-test

data:  Price_in_Lakhs by Furnished_Status
t = -0.77162, df = 166624, p-value = 0.4403
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Furnished and group Unfurnished is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -1.891114  0.822709
sample estimates:
  mean in group Furnished mean in group Unfurnished 
                 254.4455                  254.9798 



Interpretation:
Since the p-values = 0.44 >0.05, we fail to reject the null hypothesis. Thus, we can say that there is no significant difference between the prices of the houses which are furnished or unfurnished(based on the data).

6.5 Random Forest

Since our RMSE and MAE results revealed that luxury outliers and non-linear patterns are challenging for our LM and GLM, a Random Forest is the natural evolution for our project. It builds hundreds of decision trees and averages them, which should significantly reduce the high errors.



Code
library(randomForest)

set.seed(12)
train_sample <- train_data[sample(1:nrow(train_data), 30000), ]


rf_model <- randomForest(Price_in_Lakhs ~ Median_Price_Locality + Size_in_SqFt + 
                         Security + Property_Type_Villa, 
                         data = train_sample, 
                         ntree = 400, 
                         importance = TRUE)


pred_rf <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)
rmse_rf <- sqrt(mean((test_data$Price_in_Lakhs - pred_rf)^2))
mae_rf  <- mean(abs(test_data$Price_in_Lakhs - pred_rf))

The Linear Model (LM) is the most effective tool for this dataset, achieving the lowest average error with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 79.15 Lakhs.
